key_insight: An in-place photon-hopping circuit reduces logical resource costs for fault-tolerant quantum simulation of Tavis–Cummings lattices while supporting both closed- and open-system dynamics.
engineering_relevance: The resource estimates help assess fault-tolerant hardware requirements for simulating light–matter lattices, including state preparation and observable measurement.
method: Block-encode photon hopping and local light–matter exchange using ladder-operator circuits.
Use generalized quantum signal processing for closed-system evolution and retarded spectral-function estimation.
Use sampled first-order dilation for dissipative dynamics and transient photon-statistics estimation.
evidence_signal: Across three uniform-coefficient examples spanning 16–256 cavities, the controlled walk uses 4.75–8.11% fewer Toffoli gates than a matched two-register implementation and eliminates an auxiliary photon register.
watch_item: These are logical resource estimates rather than hardware demonstrations; total costs also depend on precision, state preparation, measurement, and open-system timesteps.
paper_title: Simulating closed- and open-system dynamics of Tavis--Cummings lattices on fault-tolerant quantum computers
